description:
We establish that the global population, although still growing, is expanding at a drastically slower rate and is set to peak at 9 billion by 2050, followed by rapid declines, with birthrates plummeting much faster in some parts of the world than others. When most people think about low birthrates, they usually connect them with low fertility rates, but are growing levels of infertility really the main driver for plummeting birthrates globally? There’s little evidence that’s what's driving the baby bust. So what is?

Kenya, a country of 55 million people, had one of the highest birthrates in the world four decades ago at 7.6 children per woman. Today that number has tumbled to 3.3 as decades of social policies aimed at sexual education, more women entering the workplace and changing societal attitudes around women's traditional roles have taken effect.

A record eight Arab teams will compete at the upcoming World Cup, marking a historic moment for the region’s football presence on the global stage.
From Qatar’s role as 2022 hosts to Morocco’s landmark semi-final run, Arab football has been steadily reshaping expectations at the tournament.
While Qatar failed to win a match on home soil, the Asian champions now aim to respond on away ground against top international opposition.
Egypt, the first Arab team to appear at a World Cup in 1934, remains in search of its first tournament victory despite continental success.
Algeria, Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Tunisia all carry distinct histories of breakthrough moments and unexpected results on the world stage.
Saudi Arabia’s famous win over Argentina in 2022 remains one of the tournament’s biggest shocks.
Morocco’s semi-final run in Qatar set a new benchmark for Arab and African football alike.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Asian champions Qatar have qualified for the FIFA World Cup through the qualification process for the first time in the nation's history.
Drawn in Group B alongside Canada, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Switzerland, the 2022 hosts now face a new challenge on football's biggest stage.
Head coach Julen Lopetegui described qualification as a historic achievement and said the team has earned the right to enjoy the occasion.
He stressed that Qatar must approach the tournament without pressure while remaining ambitious and competitive.
Lopetegui said every World Cup group is difficult, with opponents featuring players competing at the highest levels of the game.
He also highlighted the need to adapt to unfamiliar kick-off times and conditions, insisting there can be no excuses at a World Cup.
While acknowledging Qatar may face stronger teams on paper, he said the squad still has the ambition to compete and challenge for victories.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
More than 600 people have been left homeless after a fire swept through a densely populated neighbourhood in Kemayoran, central Jakarta. Hundreds of homes were destroyed in the blaze, which broke out on Monday night and rapidly spread through the area, forcing residents into emergency shelters.
Authorities deployed more than 30 fire trucks and over 100 personnel to bring the fire under control. Investigators are still working to determine the cause, though early indications suggest it may have been triggered by an electrical short circuit.
Displaced residents are now staying in temporary shelters where they are being provided with food, water and clothing, while others return to the site to search through the debris for belongings.
The fire highlights the recurring risk in Jakarta’s densely populated settlements, where closely packed housing and electrical faults often contribute to large-scale blazes.

Al Jazeera’s Jessica Washington reports from Jakarta.

description:
An Israeli drone strike targeted a vehicle in Khaldeh on the southern outskirts of Beirut, hitting the main highway linking the Lebanese capital to southern Lebanon. The attack occurred just a few kilometres outside Beirut on a busy route used by civilians travelling between the capital and the south. The fate of the vehicle's occupants was not immediately clear.
The strike comes ahead of a second day of talks between Israeli and Lebanese delegations in Washington, where efforts are continuing to reduce tensions and secure a broader ceasefire arrangement. It also follows comments by US President Donald Trump, who said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed not to strike near Beirut and that fighting between Israel and Hezbollah would stop.
Despite diplomatic efforts, Israel continues military operations in Lebanon, while Lebanese officials insist on a comprehensive ceasefire. The latest attack has renewed concerns that violence is edging closer to densely populated areas
title: Israeli drone hits vehicle in Khaldeh on Beirut's southern outskirts

Teachers in northeastern Nigeria have taken to the streets of Maiduguri to demand the release of 42 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State last month.
Around 1,000 members of the National Union of Teachers staged a protest, calling for stronger protection for schools, students and educators.
The demonstration highlights ongoing fears over school safety more than a decade after the mass kidnapping of schoolgirls in Chibok by Boko Haram in 2014.
Teachers say repeated attacks are undermining public confidence in education and leaving many parents fearful of sending their children to school.
Union leaders urged authorities to fully implement a safe schools initiative to protect learners, teachers and educational facilities.
The government says it is addressing the concerns, but educators warn that insecurity, conflict and displacement continue to threaten access to education across the region.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The image of the "fighter" often brings to mind a man, but women have always been present on and around the battlefield - in rebellion, defence and offence alike. Their contributions have shaped wars in ways history rarely records, and are often simplified or fetishised in popular narratives.

Around the world, women make up a far greater share of rebellions than of national armies. So what are the motivations, struggles and circumstances that drive women to take up arms and how significant is their impact on how battles are fought?

Join Ali Rae in Episode Four of All Hail the Military - a five-part series that reveals the systems, power and hidden complicities that sustain global militarism - and the profound impact it has on us all.
title: Why women go to war | All Hail the Military
